raw_case_text:
Clinical data: A 63-year-old male patient with diabetes mellitus, taking acetylsalicylic acid (100 mg) and Daonil, developed a sudden onset of headache, myalgia, anorexia, abdominal pain. Four days later he presented diarrhea, hemoptysis, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia (platelet 79.000/mm3) and hemoconcentration (hematocrit 59%). Biochemical parameters evaluated in the serum: aspartate aminotransferase 75 IU/L; alanine aminotransferase 21 IU/L; creatine phosphokinase 126 IU/L; creatinine 5.0 mg/dL; urea 57 mg/dL; lipase 41 IU/L. Ultrasonography revealed peri-hepatic and peri-pancreatic collections confirmed by computed tomography of the abdomen that also revealed: increase of the heart, discrete opacities in the left lung with marginal pleural reaction at the base of this hemithorax, distended gall bladder. Furthermore, he was submitted to routine of acute abdomen that revealed no gaseous distention. Physical examination on admission revealed blood pressure of 140/80 mmg and dehydration with cutaneous rash and petechiae. The patient presented a progressive worsening of the clinical, evolving to shock with severe pulmonary congestion, orotracheal intubation and respiratory orthesis, with the use of dopamine and dobutamine. In the next day, it was observed a hemodynamic instability and oliguria, with consequently administration of norepinephrine in increasing doses, culminating in refractory shock and death. The patient died with a clinical diagnosis of dengue hemorrhagic fever, severe ischemic cardiomyopathy and pancreatitis.
 Necropsy data: Multiple purpuric and petechial hemorrhagic lesions were evident, especially around needle puncture sites. Hemorrhages were also present in serous cavities, including hemorrhagic pleuritis (sulphation of the visceral pleura) and fibrin pericarditis. The liver and spleen were grossly congested with multiple hemorrhagic foci, and a perforated duodenal ulcer was described.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old male presenting with sudden onset of headache, myalgia, anorexia, and abdominal pain, followed by diarrhea and hemoptysis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced sudden onset of headache, myalgia, anorexia, and abdominal pain. Four days later, symptoms progressed to diarrhea, hemoptysis, and rash. Following hospital admission, he deteriorated rapidly with severe pulmonary congestion, refractory shock, hemodynamic collapse, and oliguria.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Regular home medications: acetylsalicylic acid 100 mg daily and Daonil (glibenclamide).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, myalgias, anorexia, abdominal pain, diarrhea, hemoptysis, and cutaneous rash. Home medications: acetylsalicylic acid (100 mg), Daonil. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Blood pressure: 140/80 mmHg; signs of dehydration with cutaneous rash and petechiae. Progressed to refractory shock, severe pulmonary congestion, and hemodynamic instability.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Leukopenia, thrombocytopenia (platelet count 79,000/mm3), and hemoconcentration (hematocrit 59%). Serum biochemistry: AST 75 IU/L, ALT 21 IU/L, CPK 126 IU/L, creatinine 5.0 mg/dL, urea 57 mg/dL, lipase 41 IU/L. Plain abdominal radiograph: No gaseous distention. Abdominal ultrasound: Peri-hepatic and peri-pancreatic fluid collections.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal and thoracic computed tomography (CT): Confirmed peri-hepatic and peri-pancreatic collections, cardiomegaly, discrete opacities in the left lung with marginal pleural reaction at the base of the left hemithorax, and distended gallbladder.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Fatal dengue hemorrhagic fever complicated by profound plasma leakage, severe ischemic cardiomyopathy, acute pancreatitis, acute renal failure, and perforated duodenal ulcer. Necropsy confirmation: Multiple purpuric and petechial hemorrhagic lesions, hemorrhagic pleuritis, fibrin pericarditis, gross hepatic and splenic congestion with multiple hemorrhagic foci, and a perforated duodenal ulcer.
Plan & Outcome: Managed in intensive care with orotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive infusions (dopamine, dobutamine, and escalating doses of norepinephrine). Despite aggressive resuscitation, refractory shock and anuria progressed, culminating in death.
